planting.note: Set out container-grown plants or rooted cuttings after all frost danger has passed, since this species has no cold hardiness and is grown outdoors year-round only in essentially frost-free climates.

directions: This evergreen Myrtaceae shrub to small tree is native across a swath of the South Pacific including Fiji and Vanuatu, where it grows in open, often exposed coastal and montane sites related to the better-known New Zealand pohutukawa. It produces clusters of brush-like flowers made up of long, showy stamens, most commonly in shades of red, in flushes through the warmer months on new growth. In frost-free gardens it can be grown as a sunny shrub border or specimen, but it is most widely offered in specialty nurseries as a compact, free-flowering container or patio plant, kept smaller than its wild stature through regular pruning. It tolerates light salt spray and wind, prefers well-drained soil, and benefits from reduced watering through cooler winter months to encourage bud set.
sources: Pacific Island Ecosystems at Risk (PIER), USDA Forest Service
